title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 3 questions (3.1)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A team is about to change approval schemes and segments for hundreds of access profiles. Where should the engineer test the changes FIRST?
choices: In a sandbox tenant, then promote the tested configuration to production
In production, with a note to roll back if users complain
In production, but only on access profiles that nobody has requested so far
In a spreadsheet model of the approval paths and segments
questions.answer: In a sandbox tenant, then promote the tested configuration to production
questions.explanation: A sandbox tenant lets the team test with realistic data without affecting users, and the tested configuration can then be moved with configuration management tools. Testing directly in production risks wrong approvals or visibility.

questions.stem: An engineer tests a new segment by signing in with an org admin account and finds every access item visible. What should the engineer change in the test?
choices: Disable the segment and enable it again
Add the admin account to the segment's identity criteria and sign in again
Remove the access items from all other segments
Sign in as non-admin test identities inside and outside the segment
questions.answer: Sign in as non-admin test identities inside and outside the segment
questions.explanation: Org administrators see all access items regardless of segments, so a valid test uses ordinary identities that should and should not see each item. Toggling or changing criteria does not fix a test run under the wrong user.

questions.stem: An engineer shortens the reminder schedule in Approval Settings and checks a request submitted last week, which still follows the old schedule. What is the BEST next step for the test?
choices: Cancel the old request and wait for reminders to restart
Restart the virtual appliance so the new schedule loads
Submit a new request, since changes apply only to requests created afterwards
Reassign the old request so that it picks up the new reminder settings
questions.answer: Submit a new request, since changes apply only to requests created afterwards
questions.explanation: Reminder, escalation and timeout changes only affect requests created after the change; pending requests keep their original configuration. Reassigning only restarts the existing timing.

questions.stem: A test plan for a new access profile covers manager approval for requests. Which additional test case is MOST important to include?
choices: A second request from the same user with the same justification and the same approver
A removal request and the end-to-end provisioning result on the target source
A request submitted from a different web browser
A request made outside working hours
questions.answer: A removal request and the end-to-end provisioning result on the target source
questions.explanation: A good access test covers grant and removal paths and confirms that provisioning actually changed the account on the target. Repeating identical requests adds little coverage.

questions.stem: Which evidence BEST confirms that an access request test passed end to end?
choices: The requester got the submitted email and the approver's decision email
The approver clicked Approve in the approval email
The request is complete and the target account holds the entitlement
The access profile appears in the Request Center
questions.answer: The request is complete and the target account holds the entitlement
questions.explanation: End-to-end success means the request finished and the target system reflects the change. Emails and approvals are steps along the way, not proof of provisioning.

questions.stem: A new governance group approval scheme is ready. Which test approach follows best practice?
choices: Test every approver path, including escalation and fallback, with test identities
Test only the main approver, because escalation is automatic
Ask the governance group to approve all pending production requests as the final test
Test the scheme by assigning access directly as an admin
questions.answer: Test every approver path, including escalation and fallback, with test identities
questions.explanation: Every path a request can take, including escalation and fallback, should be exercised before rollout. Direct admin assignment bypasses the approval scheme being tested.

questions.stem: A test case for a new segment checks that sales staff can see the Sales CRM access profile. Which negative test case should accompany it?
choices: A sales identity can see every other access profile
A non-sales identity cannot see the Sales CRM access profile
An org admin cannot see the Sales CRM access profile
A sales identity cannot request access for others
questions.answer: A non-sales identity cannot see the Sales CRM access profile
questions.explanation: Negative tests prove that the restriction works for users outside the segment. Org admins always see every item, and segments do not limit requesting on behalf of others.

questions.stem: Where does an engineer configure tenant-wide reminders for pending approval requests?
choices: Admin > Access Model > Segments, on each segment
Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles, on each profile's settings page
Admin > Connections > Sources, on each source's settings
Admin > Global > System Settings, under Feature Settings > Approval Settings
questions.answer: Admin > Global > System Settings, under Feature Settings > Approval Settings
questions.explanation: Global reminders, escalations and timeouts are set on the Approval Settings page under system settings. Individual access items can then override them.

questions.stem: Approvers should get the first reminder three days after a request and then one reminder a week, with no more than four reminders. Which settings achieve this?
choices: A three-day timeout, a weekly escalation frequency and four escalation steps
Start reminders after three days, frequency weekly, number of reminders four
A weekly escalation, a three-day timeout and four fallback approvers
Number of reminders set to three and a four-day reminder frequency
questions.answer: Start reminders after three days, frequency weekly, number of reminders four
questions.explanation: Reminders are configured by number of reminders, days after the request to start, frequency (daily, weekly or monthly) and time. Timeout and escalations solve other problems.

questions.stem: By default, what happens to an access request that no approver acts on?
choices: It times out after 90 days, and no reminders or escalations happen after that
It stays pending until an admin cancels it
It is approved automatically after 30 days
It is escalated back to the requester after 90 days so the requester can cancel it
questions.answer: It times out after 90 days, and no reminders or escalations happen after that
questions.explanation: Requests time out after 90 days without action by default, and 90 days is also the maximum timeout. ISC never approves a request just because no one acted.

questions.stem: Global reminders are enabled, but approvers of one critical access profile receive no reminders. The access profile's own reminder toggle was turned off earlier. What is the cause?
choices: Reminders are only ever sent for roles and entitlements, never for access profiles
The global setting applies only to entitlement requests
The item's own off setting overrides the global setting, so none are sent
Reminders need a governance group as approver to work
questions.answer: The item's own off setting overrides the global setting, so none are sent
questions.explanation: Settings on an individual access item override the global ones, and an explicit off means no reminders even when they are configured globally. The fix is to clear or reconfigure the item's setting.

questions.stem: An approver reassigns an access request to a colleague two days after the first reminder. What happens to the reminder and escalation timing?
choices: The timing continues from the original request date
Reminders stop and only escalations continue
The request is sent straight to the fallback approver
The timing restarts from the reassignment
questions.answer: The timing restarts from the reassignment
questions.explanation: Reassigning a request restarts the reminder and escalation clock for the new reviewer. This gives the new reviewer the full schedule.

questions.stem: Reminders are configured for 9:00, but approvers in Singapore receive them overnight. Which setting should the engineer check?
choices: The time zone attribute on each approver's identity
The virtual appliance's operating system clock
The time zone of the HR source's aggregation schedule
The time zone set at the bottom of the Approval Settings page
questions.answer: The time zone set at the bottom of the Approval Settings page
questions.explanation: One time zone setting on the Approval Settings page applies to all reminders and escalations. Approver identity attributes and VA clocks do not drive the schedule.

questions.stem: Escalations are enabled, but no custom escalation chain has been configured. Where do the escalations go?
choices: All escalations go to the item's source owner, then to the org admins
First two to the current reviewer's manager, then the fallback approver
The first goes to the requester, then to any org admin
All escalations go to the fallback approver right away
questions.answer: First two to the current reviewer's manager, then the fallback approver
questions.explanation: The default pattern escalates to the manager of the assigned reviewer twice and then to the fallback approver. Source owners and requesters are not default escalation targets.

questions.stem: Which reviewer categories can an engineer add to the escalation chain in Approval Settings?
choices: Manager, Identity, Governance Group and Owners
Requester, Helpdesk, Source and Segment
Identity Profile, Lifecycle State and Role
Certifier, Auditor and Report Admin
questions.answer: Manager, Identity, Governance Group and Owners
questions.explanation: The escalation chain accepts Manager, a specific Identity, a Governance Group or Owners, and a fallback approver is chosen separately. The other options are not reviewer categories.

questions.stem: When is an approval request sent to the fallback approver?
choices: When the first reminder is sent to the approver
When the requester cancels and resubmits the request after the timeout
When the escalation chain is used up, or no approver is found
When the approver approves the request partially
questions.answer: When the escalation chain is used up, or no approver is found
questions.explanation: The fallback approver is the last step after the escalation chain is exhausted, and it also receives requests when no approver can be found. Reminders do not change the assignee.

questions.stem: The identity named as fallback approver was deleted from the tenant. What happens when a request reaches the fallback step?
choices: It is approved automatically
It is denied automatically
It stays with the last valid approver
It is assigned to all org admins
questions.answer: It stays with the last valid approver
questions.explanation: If the fallback approver no longer exists, the request remains with the last valid approver. The engineer should keep the fallback approver up to date, ideally as a governance group.

questions.stem: A governance group approves requests, and the escalation chain uses the manager of each reviewer. One member has no manager. What happens at the first escalation?
choices: The whole request goes to the fallback approver for every member
The request is denied because a manager is missing
The member's assignment goes to the requester
That member keeps the assignment, while the others go to their managers
questions.answer: That member keeps the assignment, while the others go to their managers
questions.explanation: Each governance group member escalates to their own manager; a member without a manager keeps the assignment. Only when no member has a manager does the request go to the fallback approver.

questions.stem: An escalation assigns a request to an identity that has been disabled. How can an admin move the request to someone who can act on it?
choices: Re-enable and then disable the identity
Forward it with the forward access request API
Turn escalations off and back on for the item
Change the requester's lifecycle state
questions.answer: Forward it with the forward access request API
questions.explanation: Requests are assigned to the configured identity even when it is disabled or incomplete, and an admin can reassign it with the forward access request endpoint. Toggling settings does not move pending requests.

questions.stem: Security wants escalations to begin five days after a request, run every day at 8:00 and go first to the reviewer's manager and then to the IAM governance group. Which settings meet this?
choices: Escalation starts at five days, runs daily at 8:00, chain Manager then the group
A five-day timeout, daily reminders at 8:00 and the governance group set as requester
Five reminders a day starting at 8:00 with the manager as fallback approver
A daily timeout, a five-step chain and the governance group as owner
questions.answer: Escalation starts at five days, runs daily at 8:00, chain Manager then the group
questions.explanation: Escalations are set by days after the request to start, frequency, time and an ordered chain of reviewers. Timeouts and reminders handle expiry and nudges, not reassignment.

questions.stem: A company wants only employees in Germany to see the German payroll access profile in the Request Center. Which feature fits this requirement?
choices: A separation of duties policy on the access profile
A data segment that limits which admins can view and edit the access profile
An access request segment with country criteria holding the access profile
A lifecycle state that grants the access profile
questions.answer: An access request segment with country criteria holding the access profile
questions.explanation: Access request segments limit which users can see and request specific access items. Data segmentation controls admin record access, and SoD policies address toxic combinations.

questions.stem: An access profile is in no segment, while other items are restricted to segments. Who can see the unsegmented access profile in the Request Center?
choices: Only org admins and the access profile owner
Only users who belong to at least one segment
No one, until it is added to a segment
Every user who can make access requests
questions.answer: Every user who can make access requests
questions.explanation: Items that are not in any segment are requestable by anyone. To restrict an item, it must be added to a segment.

questions.stem: A manager in the Sales segment can see the Sales CRM access profile. Can the manager request it for a team member who is not in the Sales segment?
choices: Yes, if the manager is allowed to request on behalf of that person
No, because the recipient must also be in the segment
No, because segments block requests for others
Yes, but only after the team member is added to the Sales segment
questions.answer: Yes, if the manager is allowed to request on behalf of that person
questions.explanation: Segments apply to the requester's view; if the requester can see an item, they can request it for anyone they are authorized to request for. Segments are not a provisioning control.

questions.stem: Which requirement is a valid use case for access request segments?
choices: Blocking toxic combinations of finance entitlements
Showing contractors a smaller catalog of requestable access than employees
Granting access automatically to all staff in a department when they are hired
Limiting which admins can view identity records
questions.answer: Showing contractors a smaller catalog of requestable access than employees
questions.explanation: Segments tailor what each group sees in the Request Center. SoD policies, role criteria and data segmentation solve the other requirements.

questions.stem: Auditors ask whether segments stop a role from being assigned to users outside the segment through role membership criteria. What is the correct answer?
choices: Yes, segments remove access from users outside the segment
No, segments only control which items requesters see in the Request Center
Yes, segments stop role criteria from matching users outside them
No, but segments do block provisioning by lifecycle states
questions.answer: No, segments only control which items requesters see in the Request Center
questions.explanation: Segments affect request visibility, not automatic assignment, provisioning or certifications. Controls such as SoD policies and certifications address assignments made by other means.

questions.stem: Access must be visible to users in the US or Canada. Segment criteria allow one value per identity attribute. What is the BEST design?
choices: Create one segment with both country equals US and country equals Canada
Create one segment and leave the country criteria empty
Create one segment for the US and one for Canada, each with the access items
Create a role for both countries and put the role in a segment
questions.answer: Create one segment for the US and one for Canada, each with the access items
questions.explanation: Segment criteria are combined with AND and allow one value per attribute, so an OR between values needs separate segments. Empty criteria would not limit visibility to those countries.

questions.stem: Where does an engineer create an access request segment?
choices: Admin > Global > System Settings > Segments
Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles
Admin > Connections > Sources > Segments
Admin > Access Model > Segments
questions.answer: Admin > Access Model > Segments
questions.explanation: Access request segments are created under Access Model. Identity profiles provide the attributes used in segment criteria but do not hold segments.

questions.stem: Which access items can be added to an access request segment?
choices: Access profiles, entitlements and roles
Identity profiles, lifecycle states and sources
Workflows, forms and email templates
Governance groups, certifications and reports
questions.answer: Access profiles, entitlements and roles
questions.explanation: Segments hold the requestable access items users see in the Request Center: access profiles, entitlements and roles. The other options are not requestable items.

questions.stem: A segment should be based on an HR field that is not yet an identity attribute. What should the engineer do?
choices: Reference the HR account attribute directly in the segment's identity criteria
Put the HR field's values in the segment description
Create one segment per HR account with that value
Map the field to an identity attribute, then use it in the segment criteria
questions.answer: Map the field to an identity attribute, then use it in the segment criteria
questions.explanation: Segment criteria use identity attributes, so other data must first be mapped into an identity attribute. Account attributes cannot be referenced directly.

questions.stem: An engineer saves a new segment, but its access items remain visible to everyone. A full day has passed. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: Whether the segment's name is unique
Whether the access items have owners
Whether the segment is enabled
Whether the identities have a manager
questions.answer: Whether the segment is enabled
questions.explanation: A segment must be enabled before it is used with access requests, and changes can take about 20 minutes to apply. Names and owners do not change visibility.

questions.stem: An engineer needs to add 120 roles to one segment. How should the engineer proceed?
choices: Split them across three segments with 40 roles each
Add and save them in batches of no more than 50 items
Add them all at once and save the segment
Ask SailPoint Support to raise the segment item limit
questions.answer: Add and save them in batches of no more than 50 items
questions.explanation: A segment can hold many items, but only up to 50 can be added at a time, so larger sets are added in batches. Splitting into separate segments is unnecessary.

questions.stem: An engineer disables a segment that holds the Treasury access profile, which is in no other segment. What happens in the Request Center?
choices: The Treasury access profile becomes visible to all requesters
The Treasury access profile is hidden from everyone
The Treasury access profile is removed from its holders
The Treasury access profile becomes non-requestable
questions.answer: The Treasury access profile becomes visible to all requesters
questions.explanation: Once a segment is disabled, its items are visible to all requesters unless another enabled segment includes them. Disabling a segment never removes assigned access.

questions.stem: An engineer is setting up a new access request segment. Put the steps in order.
items: Create the segment with a name and description
Define the segment identities with identity attribute criteria
Add the access profiles, entitlements and roles to the segment
Review the segment and enable it
Test with non-admin identities inside and outside the segment
questions.explanation: The segment is named, given identity criteria and access, then reviewed and enabled; testing with ordinary identities follows because admins see everything.

questions.stem: Match each approval setting to what it controls.

pairs.match: Days before an untouched request expires
Maximum reminder emails sent to the approver
Ordered reviewers who receive the request when time runs out
Final reviewer after the chain is used up
Clock used for every reminder and escalation

targets_extra: Identities who can see the item in the Request Center
questions.explanation: Approval Settings combine a timeout, reminders, an escalation chain, a fallback approver and a time zone. Visibility in the Request Center is set by segments.

questions.stem: An engineer is explaining segment behaviour to the access governance team. Which TWO statements are correct?
choices: Access items that are in no segment are visible to every requester
Org admins see all access items in the Request Center regardless of segments
Segments remove access from identities that no longer match the criteria
One segment can match two values of the same attribute with an OR
Segments stop role membership criteria from assigning access
answers: Access items that are in no segment are visible to every requester
Org admins see all access items in the Request Center regardless of segments
questions.explanation: Unsegmented items are requestable by anyone and org admins always see everything. Segments never remove access or affect role assignment, and an OR between values needs separate segments.
